implementation_notes: Ruby's duck typing removes the need for a declared target, and the standard library supplies the forwarding machinery rather than expecting you to hand-write it: `extend Forwardable` plus `def_delegators :@obj, :a, :b` generates methods that delegate, and `def_delegator :@obj, :old, :new` renames while delegating - which is the adapter's translation. SimpleDelegator and DelegateClass in the delegate library forward every supported method dynamically through method_missing and can even swap the delegate with __setobj__. Hand-write a class when the translation changes arguments or semantics; use the stdlib when you only need to re-present an object under another name.
code_sketch:
require 'forwardable'

class QueueAdapter
  extend Forwardable
  def initialize(list = [])
    @list = list
  end
  def_delegator  :@list, :push, :enq      # renamed, translated member
  def_delegators :@list, :shift, :size
end
pitfalls: Forwardable generates methods at class-definition time from an accessor name and a method name; a typo fails only when the delegated method is called, and RDoc will not list delegated methods.
SimpleDelegator inherits from BasicObject through Delegator, so it lacks many Object methods, respond_to? behaves differently for private methods, and libraries expecting a real Object can break.
Delegator forwards through method_missing, which is slower than Forwardable's generated methods and leaves is_a?/instance_of? answering for the wrapper, not the delegate.
__setobj__ swapping assumes the new delegate has the same shape as the original, because the generated or forwarded methods were derived from it.

variants.name: SimpleDelegator / DelegateClass dynamic delegation
variants.implementation_notes: When the adapter must forward the whole surface of the wrapped object and override only a few members, subclass SimpleDelegator (or use DelegateClass(Foo) to build a class that delegates Foo's methods) and override just the translated members; the wrapped object arrives in the constructor and can be replaced later with __setobj__. Choose it for 'same object, one or two changed methods' and remember that everything not overridden is forwarded dynamically.
variants.code_sketch:
require 'delegate'

class UppercaseLog < SimpleDelegator
  def log(message) = super(message.upcase)   # translate one method
end

log = UppercaseLog.new(FileLogger.new)       # the rest is forwarded
pitfalls: SimpleDelegator is a BasicObject subclass: introspection differs from a normal Object and __setobj__ refuses to delegate to self.
Overridden members still reach the delegate through super; anything not covered raises NoMethodError only when called, so the adapter's contract is discovered at run time.
Dynamic forwarding hides the adapter's real surface from tooling and is slower than Forwardable's generated methods.
